title: adaptive NCCL spinback + kernel co-scheduling with KV-prefetch prioritization
author: Maya Chen
description: Context and motivation: High-concurrency tensor-parallel workloads expose two correlated classes of runtime inefficiency: (1) short-lived NCCL congestion that causes repeated retries / CPU-side spinning and hurts tail latency, and (2) small kernel launch fragmentation that amplifies kernel overheads and prevents compute/comm overlap from being effective. In practice we observed recurring p99 spikes when many microbatches interleave KV cache loads with collective all-reduce or all-gather traffic. This PR introduces a three-part runtime mitigation: adaptive NCCL spinback, a lightweight kernel co-scheduler, and a prioritized KV prefetch queue. The goals are to (a) reduce NCCL-related stalls by adaptively backing off request submission when interconnect pressure is detected, (b) reduce kernel launch noise by co-scheduling adjacent small kernels into compact launch groups, and (c) ensure critical KV shard pages for imminent microbatches are loaded earliest to avoid blocking later compute. High-level changes: - runtime/comm: adaptive spinback controller that monitors NVML GPU metrics and per-link PCIe/NCCL counters to modulate NCCL concurrency and submission pacing. - runtime/scheduler: kernel co-scheduler that groups short kernels (<200us) and applies soft affinity to keep related kernels on the same CUDA stream when safe. - runtime/kv: prioritized prefetch queue with lookahead heuristics based on microbatch trace, sequence length distribution, and model-stage affinity. - default configs behind feature flag (spinback.enabled=false by default) and a runtime toggle to roll out canary on Dedicated pools. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-9187) [x] Unit tests for spinback controller heuristics and queue ordering [x] Microbenchmarks (8xA100, 4xA40) — attached below [x] Canary rollout plan (dedicated small pool) [x] No user-facing API changes; config flags only Benchmark summary (representative): - 8xA100 80GB, TP=8, seq=2048 long prompts: p95 latency -12%, p99 latency -22%, sustained throughput +10% - 4xA40, mixed seq distribution: mean throughput +8%, p99 latency -18%, NCCL retry events down ~30% - End-to-end cost per token (approx): -6% due to improved packing and fewer wasted retries. Implementation notes and rationale: - Spinback controller: uses aggregated NVML GPU utilization + per-peer PCIe TX/RX counters (when available) and NCCL op queue depth signals. The controller computes a moving average of link pressure and enters a lightweight spinback mode where submission threads yield for a short, adaptive window; windows grow if retries persist. This avoids hard sleeps that would break low-latency workloads. - Co-scheduler: implemented as a best-effort grouping pass immediately before kernel launches. It keeps safety checks (no cross-stream hazard for kernels that write shared buffers). Grouping targets kernels shorter than 200us and caps grouped-launch latency to 1ms to preserve soft latency SLOs. - KV prefetch prioritization: trace-based lookahead populates a priority queue; items predicted to be referenced in the next N microbatches are promoted. We added heuristics for short-sequence vs long-sequence workloads to avoid overfetch. Rollout and safeguards: - All features are hidden behind runtime flags. Canary rollout plan included A/B rollout on Dedicated pool and metrics gating on p99 latency and NCCL retries. Operator-visible knobs: spinback.target_gpu_util, spinback.max_backoff_ms, kv.prefetch_lookahead. Files changed (high-level): - runtime/comm/nccl_spinback.cpp - runtime/comm/nccl_spinback.h - runtime/scheduler/kernel_coscheduler.cpp - runtime/scheduler/kernel_coscheduler.h - runtime/scheduler/coscheduler_tests.cpp - runtime/kv/prefetcher.rs - runtime/kv/prefetch_tests.rs - runtime/config/runtime_flags.yaml - tools/perf/bench_tp_spinback.py - docs/ops/canary-rollout-spinback.md - pkg/telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml - infra/ci/flake-whitelist.yaml Commits (summary): - add adaptive NCCL spinback controller, initial heuristics and unit tests - implement kernel co-scheduler + safety checks and microbench harness - kv prefetcher: prioritized queue, lookahead heuristics, and tests - perf: bench scripts and aggregated perf reports for A100/A40 clusters - docs: rollout guide and runtime flag docs Why this is different from previous work: Earlier patches focused on static stream prioritization and coarse NCCL concurrency caps. This change couples live hardware telemetry (NVML/PCIE) with submission backoff and adds kernel-level co-scheduling that reduces launch fragmentation. The prioritized KV prefetcher ties the scheduler and cache subsystems together so prefetches align to grouped launches, reducing head-of-line stalls. Test plan and perf validation: - Unit tests for controller logic and queue ordering (added test vectors for increasing/decreasing pressure). - Integration perf runs on internal perf lab: 8xA100 80GB (TP=8/TP=16) and 4xA40 mixed sequences. Results attached in bench artifacts. - Canary plan: 48h canary on Dedicated pool with alerting thresholds: p99 increase > 5% or NCCL retry rate > baseline triggers rollback. Ops notes: - New telemetry: nccl_spinback_events, spinback_backoff_ms, kv_prefetch_promotions, coscheduler_group_count. These are added to metrics_definitions for alerting and dashboards. Potential follow-ups: - Integrate RDMA and fabric-level counters when available to improve link pressure prediction. - Extend co-scheduling to multi-node grouping when microbatch alignment is known.
release_notes: Adds adaptive NCCL backoff, kernel co-scheduler, and prioritized KV prefetch behind feature flags; reduces p99 in TP runs; opt-in canary rollout for Dedicated pools.
